newFindings.subject: Wrapper registry pattern for monkeypatch-safe file split
newFindings.detail: ielts-vocab Task 5 discovered that splitting a Python module across multiple files breaks monkeypatch-based unit tests. The old single-module pattern worked because monkeypatch.setattr(module, 'X', ...) wrote to module globals which all functions read directly. After split, each function lives in a different module; patching the wrapper module's globals no longer affects the inner module's reads. Solution: a thin _wrapper_registry.py that binds the wrapper module's __dict__ to a property, and each submodule reads from the wrapper at call time. This is a reusable pattern for future Python file-split refactors in the workspace.
newFindings.resolution: Pattern codified in /Volumes/code/workspace/products/ielts-vocab/packages/platform-sdk/platform_sdk/_wrapper_registry.py (44 lines). Documented in Task 5 report. Could be promoted to foundation/axi-rules as a Python-style rule if encountered again.

newFindings.subject: axi-submit-log-post-commit hook produces persistent dirty worktrees
newFindings.detail: axi-submit-log-post-commit hook (axi-workspace-git-hooks module) writes a new docs/logs/submit/<ISO>-auto-submit.md file after every commit. This file is not auto-tracked, not auto-gitignored, and accumulates as untracked work. 4+ repos now carry these files. Per AR-GIT-003 the intended lifecycle is periodic absorb (commit `docs(logs): absorb session submit logs`), but no cron / hook enforces this. M17 patched 3-4 individual repos with per-repo gitignore but did not address the root cause.
newFindings.resolution: Recorded as OD-M17-AUTOSUBMIT-ROOT-CAUSE for owner disposition. Three options surfaced: (a) close the hook entirely (sacrifice audit trail), (b) make hook dry-run in dev (keep rule, suppress output), (c) add docs/logs/submit/*.md to root-level /Volumes/code/workspace/.gitignore (cosmetic-only since each repo has its own .gitignore).
